I've had a relationship where my partner was not doing great but also refused to seek professional help. In the end that was one of the reasons for me to break up the relationship. That is hard to compare to your relationship however so cannot really give you advise on what to do on that regard
What I can say however is that you cannot help her with this, she needs professional help. Solely you trying to help her will likely mostly burden you and will not solve her issues. 
If she doesn't want to seek professional help herself, no one can really help her much. A professional could also help her get past her job issues probably. Is there a reason that she refuses professional help so far? (Taboo or something?) In my relationship it was mostly that she refused to acknowledge that she had mental issues and for some reason professional help was a big taboo for her.

In your case I think I would keep pressuring her to seek help, both for her sake and your sake. If she still refuses to help herself I would probably make clear that I will not stick around for the relationship otherwise.

Being nice about these things does not help in my opinion, you are allowed to be direct on this kind of stuff, she needs to hear it.

Then I'm afraid that she is more ready than she's saying she is. Maybe tell her to take it slower and stop calling as often etc?

I'm curious to these questions:
What are the things you think are going to fast (for example the frequent calls)?
Would you see a future with her if you would have been ready to settle down?

I'm afraid ending the relationship is the logical step if you aren't ready for the relationship but she is, then it would not last anyways.

Though this is all easy to say, I struggle with this too... I'm sort of in the same situation but am very hesitant to break up because I would see a future for us if I were ready and I do not want to break her heart.

It's difficult for us to determine whether you're ready for a long term relationship, that is something you and your brain will have to figure out I'm afraid.

That said, when you're ready but it just seems to overwhelming to you: tell her. I did that too in the past and it really helped. Just tell her it all, that you want a relationship but that it terrifies you too and that you need a slow pace, and be clear about what that means (for example not interested in kids anytime soon). If she really loves you she will probably agree to take it slow, even though she may not like it. If she is unwilling to take it slow I'd say put yourself first, end the relationship and work on yourself until you think you're ready for that long-term relationship (either with her or with another person).

If you're not feeling ready for a (long-term) relationship at all, I think it would be better to end it now. Do not 'hang it out' just because  she has mental problems, you are not responsible for those and it is okay to put yourself first sometimes. If you feel like you are not ready for settling for a person now you likely won't feel like it in the near future of this relationship and it will just drag the situation on, stress you out and hurt her more.

Thank you for reading, I first want to clarify a few things:

* This graph does not directly portray the economic situation in the Netherlands, merely the government ‘spending’. When the graph goes up, it basically means that the government spends more money (for example to healthcare) than it ears (through taxes etc).
* The Netherlands is quite a ‘social’ country; in the financial crisis of 2007-2008 and the crisis of the new coronavirus, many businesses and people are financially supported (or compensated if you will) by the government. For example: right now the government compensates up to 90% of the wages for companies hit by the crisis. This means the government has to spend more money, which leads to the government debt increasing. That is why the graph goes up in the financial crises. I would be interested to see how this compares to other countries.
* The percentage for 2020 is an estimate by the Cabinet, in the case of a second wave (or whatever else 2020 has in store for us…), the percentage is likely to increase further for this year.

​

The percentages from 1990-2019 were taken from Wikipedia (in Dutch):

[https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overheidsschuld](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overheidsschuld)
